_comment: Carry destination for issue #954's one follow-up still owed after its checklist landed.
W4D-G9, the roster group that covered #954, is at resume.stage done, so it is not a
destination (PR #1098); PR #1072's carry moved here from that group's brief in the #954
close-out record pull request, which also closes #954. Shape and required fields:
stage: The tools/release/stamp.py change owed once main-protect's bypass was narrowed to the deploy key (decision 0009 steps 5 and 6): a stamp that pushes must name --push-key, refused before it writes anything otherwise. #954 is closed, so no open issue tracks this stage; this file does.

carries.from: PR #1072 (deploy-key stamping), its round-2 review; moved from W4D-G9's done brief by the #954 close-out record pull request
carries.control: A direct push to main now lands only over the deploy key. Step 5's probe (#201 comment 5704665628), on a throwaway branch under a throwaway ruleset carrying the planned bypass list: an API ref update as tvofi (admin) was refused, the same as tvofi-seat-author (write), and a push over the deploy key landed; the refused arms are the null control for the landed one. Step 6 then removed the admin bypass altogether (comment 5708908916), and v6.6.0 was stamped over the key (comment 5708985902). The keyless stamp --push sites PR #1072's review listed under .claude/workflows were moved to --push-key by PR #1077: fragments_sync.mjs reports no tracked stamp --push without --push-key, and its self-test reports a bent keyless stamp text while passing the same text with the key, so the clean reading is not a scan over nothing.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base: run node .claude/workflows/fragments_sync.mjs, and git grep -n -- '--push' .claude/workflows, and read rulesets/22628467 with a token that can see bypass_actors before assuming the deploy key is still the only bypass. Read main() in tools/release/stamp.py for how a push without a key is handled today rather than trusting this carry.
carries.brief: Resolved, and not to be redone: the step-5 precondition (no stamp path pushing without the key, met by PR #1077), the web prompts naming --push-key, and the re-run of the probe arms after the narrowing. Still owed, in tools/release/stamp.py: a push without a key is refused by the stamp itself. Until that lands a keyless push is refused only by the ruleset, after the stamp has committed and tagged locally, and its except arm discards both; refusing it in argument handling moves the refusal before anything is written. Legitimate only while the ruleset's sole bypass is the deploy key, which is the remeasure step's reading. The refusal names --push-key and --known-hosts, and the stamp's --self-test carries both arms: the keyless push refused, the keyed one accepted.
